title: Tenant occupancy radar, long-request detection, and prefill isolation follow-up
creator: Ava Chen
description:
During the 2026-02-27 hosted GPU saturation incident we observed sustained queue buildup from a small set of tenants running long-kernel/image-generation jobs that heavily polluted the KV cache and kept slots occupied past autoscaler thresholds. This ticket tracks the postmortem actions and engineering work to reduce similar incidents.

Goals:
- Detect long-running, cache-heavy requests quickly and isolate them from slot priming flows.
- Avoid cache pollution and ensure fair slot reuse across tenants.
- Make autoscaler reactive to tail occupancy and reduce oscillation.

Proposed action items:
1) Long-request detector: add a probe at admission to mark requests with expected token-length or estimated compute-duration; record to telemetry and surface alerts for >90th percentile durations.
2) Prefill isolation: prevent in-flight prefetch/prefill for tenants flagged as 'long-running' by routing them to dedicated warm lanes with bounded concurrency.
3) KV cache TTL & eviction rules: implement tenant-aware cache lanes and short TTL for ephemeral image-generation keys; add metrics for cache hit-rate by tenant.
4) Autoscaler hysteresis tuning: lower react window for tail occupancy, add 'occupied-slot-weight' metric that distinguishes idle vs compute-occupied slots.
5) Rapid fallback model path: implement policy to serve large requests on quantized/model-variant nodes when pool saturated to reduce per-request GPU time.
6) Synthetic stress tests: add tenant-burst scenarios to the capacity simulator, validate admission and autoscaler behavior.
7) Instrumentation and dashboards: new 'tenant occupancy radar' dashboard with heatmap of long-requests, per-tenant KV hit/miss, and slot-duration percentiles.
8) Runbook updates: add steps to detect, isolate, and reroute long-run workloads; include customer comms template.

Acceptance criteria:
- Long-request detector firing with <30s median detection time on synthetic runs.
- Autoscaler shows 25% reduction in tail slot occupancy during test scenarios.
- No regressions in P95 latency for standard short-text workloads.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Routing long runs to dedicated warm lanes increases operational cost; will scope by tenant score and offer opt-in reserved lanes for high-paying users.
- Shortening KV TTL may reduce cache efficiency for benign workloads; we will A/B with traffic and monitor embedding cost.

Owners:
- Miguel Torres (engineer owner)
- Priya Patel (SRE lead)
- Lina Gomez (Product)

Timeline:
- Prototype long-request detector + dashboard: 2 sprints
- Prefill isolation and autoscaler tuning: 3 sprints
- KV eviction and model-variant routing: 2 sprints

comments: 2026-03-01: Initial triage. Confirmed region us-west-2 experienced prolonged slot occupancy caused by 3 tenants running heavy image-gen pipelines. KV cache hit-rate dropped by 40% for those tenants, causing excessive re-prefill and slot holding. - Ava

2026-03-02: Miguel created a lightweight admission probe that timestamps request phases. Early synthetic runs reproduce tail occupancy at 10k qps. PR opened for detector prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1118 - Miguel

2026-03-04: SRE observed autoscaler reaction lag around 90s due to hysteresis window tuned for throughput stability. Agreed to try lowering scale-up window for 'occupied-slot-weight' metric in a canary. - Priya

2026-03-05: Design review: Lina suggested tenant-scoring to gate which customers get routed to dedicated warm lanes. Product requested opt-in reserved lanes for large enterprise customers to avoid cost shifting. - Lina

2026-03-07: Ran capacity-sim tenant-burst tests (scenario B3) with prototype detector + isolation. Tail occupancy reduced by ~28% in sims; KV hit-rate improved for short-text traffic. Logged telemetry to new radar dashboard. - Miguel

2026-03-09: Security review flagged model-variant routing for potential data-mixing risk. Decided to require per-tenant isolation and KMS keys for any model variant shift. Security review ticket created. - Priya

2026-03-10: Next steps: finalize detector PR, create feature flag for prefill isolation, schedule autoscaler tuning in next ops window, and add runbook section for manual isolation and customer communication template. - Ava
